skill.name: hypogenic
skill.description: Generates and evaluates scientific hypotheses from observational datasets, with optional literature integration through HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, and union workflows.
skill.summary: Generate testable hypotheses from data and research literature.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 94 static findings are false positives: the scanner interpreted Markdown backticks, explicit documentation links, and an environment-variable name as executable behavior. The source contains no executable scripts, hidden network activity, or prompt injection instructions. Two medium semantic risks remain: API processing can disclose sensitive records, and direct data interpolation permits prompt injection into research outputs.

remediation.issue: API-backed models may receive sensitive research records.
remediation.suggestion: Document provider retention terms, remove direct identifiers, obtain required consent, and prefer local models for sensitive datasets.

remediation.issue: Dataset text is inserted directly into LLM prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Delimit dataset content, label it as untrusted, reject embedded instructions, and validate outputs before using them in research conclusions.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive records may be sent to external LLM providers
semantic_findings.description: The workflow supports API-hosted models and inserts dataset samples into inference prompts. Sensitive records could leave the local environment without de-identification or provider review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly support API-based models and interpolate sample text into prompts. Actual disclosure depends on the selected model and dataset.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted dataset text can alter model instructions
semantic_findings.description: Prompt templates interpolate data directly without marking it as untrusted. Adversarial records could redirect model behavior and corrupt generated observations or inference labels.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template directly embeds data_samples and sample_text with no content boundary or instruction hierarchy. Downstream protections are not present in the audited files.

content.value_statement: Manual hypothesis exploration is slow and difficult to scale. Hypogenic combines datasets, research papers, and LLM refinement to produce testable candidate hypotheses.
actual_capabilities: Guides data-driven hypothesis generation with the HypoGeniC method.
Explains literature-informed HypoRefine and union workflows.
Defines dataset naming, feature, label, and split requirements.
Provides configuration templates for generation, inference, relevance checks, and adaptive refinement.
Shows CLI and Python workflows for generation and multi-hypothesis inference.
Explains PDF preprocessing with GROBID for literature-based methods.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and templates, but it does not include the Hypogenic implementation.
API-backed models may add cost and send research records to external providers.
Literature workflows require local PDF files, GROBID, and additional preprocessing tools.
Generated hypotheses require expert review and do not establish causal relationships.

use_cases.title: Explore patterns in labeled data
use_cases.description: Generate measurable hypotheses from observational examples, then compare their validation performance.

use_cases.title: Connect literature with empirical evidence
use_cases.description: Extract insights from papers and refine them against a prepared research dataset.

use_cases.title: Build a reproducible hypothesis benchmark
use_cases.description: Configure dataset splits, prompts, inference methods, and evaluation metrics for repeated experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starting workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my research question, dataset columns, labels, and available literature. Recommend HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, or union, and explain the required inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginning a new hypothesis generation project

prompt_templates.title: Prepare the dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the train, validation, and test structure for [task]. Map [features] and [labels] to Hypogenic fields, and identify validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design literature-informed prompts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create prompt specifications for [research domain] using [dataset] and [papers]. Include generation, relevance, inference, and adaptive refinement requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a comparative experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reproducible comparison of HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, and union methods for [task]. Define controls, metrics, ablations, error analysis, and reporting criteria.

output_examples.input: A labeled collection of human-written and AI-generated articles with no literature set.
output_examples.output: Recommended method: HypoGeniC. Prepare three dataset splits, define a strict label extractor, generate candidate linguistic hypotheses, and compare validation accuracy.

output_examples.input: Ten deception studies and labeled hotel reviews with genuine and fraudulent classes.
output_examples.output: Recommended method: HypoRefine. Process the papers, generate literature-grounded candidates, refine them against reviews, and compare both hypothesis banks.

output_examples.input: A request to compare data-only, literature-only, and combined hypothesis quality.
output_examples.output: Experiment outline: use fixed splits and model settings, measure accuracy and diversity, record costs, inspect failure cases, and report method-specific limitations.

best_practices: Keep training, validation, and test splits separate throughout hypothesis generation and evaluation.
Use precise label formats and test the extraction function before full experiments.
Review generated hypotheses for novelty, testability, bias, and domain validity.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated hypotheses as proven findings or causal evidence.
Do not send identifiable or restricted data to external models without approval.
Do not tune prompts or hypotheses against the final test set.

faq.question: What methods does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers data-driven HypoGeniC, literature-integrated HypoRefine, and union methods that combine separate hypothesis banks.

faq.question: What data format is required?
faq.answer: Use separate training, validation, and test files with text feature lists and matching label lists.

faq.question: Does the skill install Hypogenic?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation and usage guidance for the external Hypogenic package.

faq.question: Can I use local language models?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation states that Hypogenic supports API-based and local models, subject to your package configuration.

faq.question: When is GROBID required?
faq.answer: GROBID is required when preprocessing research PDFs for HypoRefine or union workflows.

faq.question: Are generated hypotheses scientifically validated?
faq.answer: No. They are candidates that require empirical testing, expert review, and careful reporting of uncertainty.
